newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end firm, but fails to break barrier.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end firm, but fails to break barrier.

text.p: The Philippine stock index settled higher for the eighth straight session on Wednesday, propped up by buying in several blue chip issues, traders said.

"We have been seeing a slow rise. It's better because it's more enduring, more solid. The peso-dollar rate seems to have settled at 28.56 pesos to a dollar and that's encouraging news for the market," said Irving Ackerman, president at I. Ackerman & Co Inc.
The composite index closed 18.59 points, or 0.69 percent, higher at 2,694.79. It threatened to break the 2,700 psychological barrier but encountered stiff resistance.

"The market's really oversold. With the Thailand crisis seemingly over and done with, the currency situation in the region is improving and it's good for the stock market," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development.
Manila Electric Co B led blue chip issues, closing seven pesos higher, or 5.34 percent, at 138 pesos.
Thirdliner issues such as Liberty Telecoms Holdings Inc which posted gains in recent days gave in to profit-taking.
Liberty which denied rumours of joint venture talks with Bayan Telecommunications Holdings Corp, a unit of Benpres Holdings Corp, settled 25 centavos lower, or 25.77 percent, at 72 centavos.
Turnover slightly improved to 2.14 billion pesos compared with 2.018 billion the previous day. Gainers in the broad market outnumbered losers 71 to 46 with 59 unchanged issues.

"Most blue chips especially Meralco are being accumulated. The market has been on the rise for several days. We might see some correction tomorrow," said Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities.
